title: Finish the type check
starter:
let result_dtype (op : string) (a : string) (b : string) : string =
  match op with
  | "add" | "mul" | "max" | "xor" -> if a = b then a else "rejected"
  | "cmplt" -> a
  | "div" | "mod" | "shl" -> "i32"
  | _ -> "rejected"
hints: Each broken branch needs a check before it answers, like the `a = b` check in the first branch.
For `cmplt` the result does not depend on `a`: comparing two `i32` values gives a `bool`.
`if a = b then "bool" else "rejected"` for `cmplt`, and `if a = "i32" && b = "i32" then "i32" else "rejected"` for the last three.
explain: Each op has one rule. `add`, `mul`, `max` and `xor` need two operands of the same dtype and give that dtype back. `cmplt` needs the same, but its answer is a yes or a no, so the result is always `bool`. `div`, `mod` and `shl` only make sense on numbers, so both operands must be `i32`. Anything else is refused before the program runs.
